<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919915_theRebbe_134" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919915_theRebbe_134__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header of the maamar, including the Torah portion, date, and year.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Eikev,</t>
    <t s="2">20 Menachem-Av</t>
    <t s="3">(Maamar 2),</t>
    <t s="4">the year 5727 (1967)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse "And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear..." and the Gemara's question and answers about fear being a small matter.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you but to fear..." etc.</t>
    <t s="1">And it is brought in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="2">"Is fear then a small matter?"</t>
    <t s="3">(And it answers)</t>
    <t s="4">"Yes, relative to Moshe it is a small matter."</t>
    <t s="5">And the precise point in this is known,</t>
    <t s="6">for it is written "ask of you"</t>
    <t s="7">(from each and every Jew),</t>
    <t s="8">and what is the answer "relative to Moshe it is a small matter"?</t>
    <t s="9">Also, one must understand what is brought in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="10">"A person is obligated to recite one hundred blessings every day, as it is said, 'And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you,'</t>
    <t s="11">do not read it as 'mah' (what) but rather as 'me'ah' (one hundred)."</t>
    <t s="12">And the Maharsha wrote</t>
    <t s="13">that the reason for this, that they expounded "do not read it as 'mah' etc.," is</t>
    <t s="14">because according to the simple interpretation it is difficult: "Is fear then a small matter?" Therefore they expounded "do not read it as 'mah' but rather as 'me'ah',"</t>
    <t s="15">for this thing</t>
    <t s="16">(to recite one hundred blessings every day)</t>
    <t s="17">is easy for a person to fulfill,</t>
    <t s="18">and through this he will come to fear Hashem.</t>
    <t s="19">And explanation is needed:</t>
    <t s="20">What is the virtue of one hundred blessings, through which one comes to fear Hashem?</t>
    <t s="21">And also, one must understand,</t>
    <t s="22">according to what is known that all the interpretations of that same verse are connected to each other,</t>
    <t s="23">what is the connection between "mah" and "me'ah"?</t>
    <t s="24">And also, what is the connection between the two aforementioned interpretations</t>
    <t s="25">(which answer the difficulty "Is fear then a small matter?"),</t>
    <t s="26">namely "relative to Moshe it is a small matter" and "do not read it as 'mah' but rather as 'me'ah'."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the differences between the simple interpretation of "mah" and the expounded interpretation of "me'ah," highlighting their seemingly opposite natures.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the difference between the interpretation according to its simple meaning</t>
    <t s="2">("mah")</t>
    <t s="3">and the interpretation expounded through the study of "do not read it"</t>
    <t s="4">("me'ah"),</t>
    <t s="5">is that according to the simple interpretation,</t>
    <t s="6">"mah" refers to "to fear" etc.,</t>
    <t s="7">that all that Hashem asks of you is to fear Hashem,</t>
    <t s="8">whereas according to the expounded interpretation,</t>
    <t s="9">"mah"</t>
    <t s="10">("me'ah")</t>
    <t s="11">is a matter in itself,</t>
    <t s="12">that what Hashem asks of you is "mah,"</t>
    <t s="13">one hundred blessings,</t>
    <t s="14">except that through this you will come to fear Hashem.</t>
    <t s="15">And there is another difference between the two interpretations:</t>
    <t s="16">the word "mah" indicates that the matter</t>
    <t s="17">(under discussion)</t>
    <t s="18">is a small thing,</t>
    <t s="19">in the language of the Gemara "a small matter,"</t>
    <t s="20">whereas "me'ah" is a large number, even the completeness of number,</t>
    <t s="21">for in letters,</t>
    <t s="22">the largest number is hundreds.</t>
    <t s="23">And particularly according to what is explained in Chassidus,</t>
    <t s="24">that what is added in "me'ah" over "mah" is the letter aleph, the letter of wonder,</t>
    <t s="25">the Or HaSovev (Surrounding Light) that is above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="26">And one must understand,</t>
    <t s="27">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="28">these two differences between the two interpretations</t>
    <t s="29">are opposites.</t>
    <t s="30">For from the fact that the one hundred blessings are a preparation for fear,</t>
    <t s="31">it is understood</t>
    <t s="32">that fear is above them,</t>
    <t s="33">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="34">the obligation of one hundred blessings is learned from the exposition "do not read it as 'mah' but rather as 'me'ah',"</t>
    <t s="35">and regarding fear it is written "mah etc. asks of you,"</t>
    <t s="36">for the word "mah" indicates</t>
    <t s="37">(as above)</t>
    <t s="38">a small thing.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
